fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`AGENTS.md` lines 235-242 describe the close's completion precheck inaccurately, and agents reason
from the stated mechanism. The current text:

> **After the change MERGES, fast-forward YOUR worktree before you close.** The close's
> completion precheck reads your worktree's git history and requires the merged
> `rebar-ticket: <id>` commit reachable from HEAD (else it fails with "cannot confirm the work
> landed").

Verified against the implementation on this tree (HEAD `1052bc856f`):

1. **"the MERGED commit" is wrong.** `_referencing_commit_exists`
   (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:149`) runs
   `["git", "-C", str(repo_root), "log", "--format=%B%x00"]` (`:159-163`) with **no ref
   argument**, so it scans the whole history reachable from the current HEAD and returns True for
   ANY commit whose message carries a `rebar-ticket:` trailer or a leading `<id>:` subject that
   `resolve_ticket_id` maps into `accepted_ids` (`:170-176`). Merge status is never consulted. An
   unlanded local commit on your own branch satisfies it.
2. **The precheck is conditional; the doc presents it as unconditional.** It is guarded by
   `if field_reads.file_impact(ticket_id, tracker) and not _referencing_commit_exists(...)`
   (`transition_close.py:283-284`), so a ticket with no recorded `file_impact` never reaches it.
   It is also inside `_completion_precheck` (`:195`), which returns early when the
   `require_completion_verification_for_close` gate is off (`:228-236`), on `--force-close`
   (`:237`), and on a live duplicate/supersedes replacement link (`:256`).
3. **`accepted_ids` is a subtree, not one id.** `:277-286` adds every transitive descendant
   returned by `list_descendants` across the `epics`/`stories`/`tasks`/`bugs` buckets, so a
   parent is satisfied by a commit referencing any child.
4. **`--ref` is absent from AGENTS.md.** `rebar transition --ref=<ref>` is documented at
   `src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt:7` ("verify (and sign) against the committed tree at <ref>
   instead of HEAD. Use it to close a stacked story against its own commit while your worktree
   stays at the epic tip; default HEAD") and at `docs/plan-review-gate.md:899-916`, whose
   "Stacked-epic recipe" is exactly the workflow this repo runs. AGENTS.md never mentions it —
   `grep -n -- "--ref" AGENTS.md` returns nothing.

The fast-forward advice is a safe superset, so nobody following it is broken. The harm is the
false mechanism: believing the precheck ENFORCES land-then-close leads agents to skip `--ref` when
closing a stacked story, and to tell operators that a pre-land close is impossible. This happened
live — a session told the operator that seven in-progress epic bugs could not be closed before
landing; the operator corrected it. The rule that actually orders land-before-close is the POLICY
line one bullet above, at `AGENTS.md:233-234`: "Do **not** close a ticket until its change is
`Verified +1` — a passing completion-verifier is **not** a substitute for green CI."

## Approach

Rewrite the bullet to state the real mechanism and cite the real ordering rule, keeping the
fast-forward guidance for the case it genuinely addresses.

The corrected bullet will:

- lead with the POLICY (`Verified +1`, already stated at `AGENTS.md:233-234`) as the reason to
  wait, instead of implying the precheck enforces it;
- state the precheck accurately: when the ticket records `file_impact` and the
  completion-verification close gate is on, the close requires a commit **reachable from your
  current HEAD** carrying a `rebar-ticket:` trailer for the ticket **or any transitive
  descendant** — merge status is not checked, so a local unlanded commit satisfies it;
- keep the fast-forward recipe (`git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main`) as the
  remedy for the case it actually fixes: a worktree whose history does NOT contain the commit —
  a fresh worktree, or closing from a checkout that never had it;
- name `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --ref <sha>` as the sanctioned way to close a
  stacked story against its own commit while the worktree stays at the epic tip, and link
  `docs/plan-review-gate.md` §"Which commit the completion gate verifies — `--ref`" for the
  detail, per this file's stated "keep this file lean … one-line pointers into `docs/`" rule
  (`AGENTS.md:9-11`);
- state precisely what `--ref` does and does not do: it retargets the completion **verification
  and signature** to that ref's tree; it does **not** narrow the referencing-commit scan, which
  runs `git log` with no ref regardless (`transition_close.py:159-163`);
- preserve the existing NEVER-fast-forward-the-shared-main-checkout warning **verbatim**, as the
  final sentences of the bullet (`AGENTS.md:239-242`).

**Why a rewrite in place rather than a pointer to `docs/`.** AGENTS.md is loaded at launch by
every harness, so a wrong mechanism there is the default belief for every agent in the repo; a
pointer alone would leave the false statement resident in context. The corrected text stays short
and defers the `--ref` detail to `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, which already documents it correctly
at lines 899-916 — no new doc is created and no existing doc is duplicated.

**The whole population, not one sample.** The same misstatement exists in a second place:
`CONTRIBUTING.md:219-230` (§2f "After merge — fast-forward your worktree, THEN close the ticket")
says the precheck "requires the merged `rebar-ticket: <id>` commit to be reachable from HEAD;
without the fast-forward it fails with 'cannot confirm the work landed.'" `AGENTS.md:203` sends
readers to CONTRIBUTING.md for "the full recipe", so fixing only AGENTS.md would leave the
authoritative long-form copy wrong. `grep -rn "cannot confirm the work landed" . --exclude-dir=.git`
returns exactly one Markdown hit, `CONTRIBUTING.md:226`, alongside the source string it quotes at
`transition_close.py:291` — so those two Markdown passages ARE the population, and both are in
scope. `templates/rebar-usage.md` and `templates/AGENTS.md` do not carry the claim (the
`test_client_template_sync.py` drift gate covers only the marked rebar-usage region and forbids
Gerrit content in it), so they are untouched.

## Scope

- `AGENTS.md` — the single bullet at lines 235-242, rewritten as described above. No other line of
  the file changes.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — §2f, lines 219-230: the same three corrections (not-merged, conditional,
  `--ref`), with the blockquote warning at lines 228-230 preserved verbatim.

No file under `src/` and no test file is edited. This is a documentation-accuracy change with no
behaviour change, so there is no new testable behaviour to cover with a new test; the verification
is that the existing doc-consistency tests still pass and that the corrected text matches the
implementation, checked by the greps in the acceptance criteria below.

Assumption checked, not assumed: no test pins the wording being replaced.
`tests/unit/test_codex_agent_guidance.py:11-13` slices AGENTS.md between `"**Codex Gerrit workflow
rule:"` and `"\n\n## Record your work"`, which ends well before line 235;
`tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py` and
`tests/unit/test_serena_grep_reminder_hook.py:166-167` assert only on the "Navigating the
codebase" table; `tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py` asserts only the DCO placeholder pattern.
None reads the Git-workflow bullet or CONTRIBUTING.md §2f.

## Testing

No new test: nothing executable changes, and the module-size / doc-drift gates that do read these
files are already in the suite. Verification is by targeted grep assertions (each exits non-zero on
failure) plus the existing suite:

- `! grep -n "requires the merged" AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md` — the false claim is gone from both.
- `grep -q -- "--ref" AGENTS.md` — the stacked-close tool is now named.
- `grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" AGENTS.md && grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" CONTRIBUTING.md`
  — the shared-main-checkout warning survives in both (the phrase is on `AGENTS.md:241` and
  `CONTRIBUTING.md:229` today).
- `pytest tests/unit/test_codex_agent_guidance.py tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py
  tests/unit/test_serena_grep_reminder_hook.py tests/unit/test_client_template_sync.py
  tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py` — the doc-reading tests still pass.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — unaffected, run to confirm exit 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The AGENTS.md bullet no longer claims the precheck requires a MERGED commit; verified by
      `! grep -n "requires the merged" AGENTS.md` exiting 0 (no match).
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md §2f no longer makes the same claim; verified by
      `! grep -n "requires the merged" CONTRIBUTING.md` exiting 0 (no match).
- [ ] The AGENTS.md bullet states that the precheck runs only when the ticket records
      `file_impact`; verified by `grep -q "file_impact" AGENTS.md` exiting 0.
- [ ] The AGENTS.md bullet states that a referencing commit for the ticket OR any transitive
      descendant satisfies the check; verified by `grep -q "descendant" AGENTS.md` exiting 0 and
      by reading the bullet against `transition_close.py:277-286`.
- [ ] The AGENTS.md bullet documents `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --ref <sha>` as the
      way to close a stacked story against its own commit without moving the worktree; verified by
      `grep -q -- "--ref" AGENTS.md` exiting 0 (it matches nothing today).
- [ ] The land-before-close ordering is attributed to the `Verified +1` policy rule rather than to
      the precheck; verified by the rewritten bullet naming `Verified +1` — `grep -c "Verified +1"
      AGENTS.md` is one greater than its current value of 3.
- [ ] The NEVER-fast-forward-the-shared-main-checkout warning is preserved verbatim in both files;
      verified by `grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" AGENTS.md` and
      `grep -q "uncommitted operator WIP" CONTRIBUTING.md` both exiting 0, and by
      `git diff AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md` showing those warning sentences unchanged.
- [ ] No source or test file is modified; verified by `git diff --name-only origin/main` listing
      exactly `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [ ] The doc-reading tests still pass; verified by `pytest
      tests/unit/test_codex_agent_guidance.py tests/unit/test_agents_serena_untyped_receiver.py
      tests/unit/test_serena_grep_reminder_hook.py tests/unit/test_client_template_sync.py
      tests/unit/test_check_dco_identity.py` exiting 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0 and `make typecheck` exits 0.
